catalog_quote: [p.63] Syllables with a central vowel nucleus appear to take stress. Nmbo stress is obligatory, and tends to fall on the penultimate syllable. Many multisyllabic Nmbo words that take stress do not contain full vowels, e.g., ytqn [jɐtk͡pɐn] ‘name’(135), kkv [kɐkɐβ] ‘garden’(136). ... [p.66] While I describe Nmbo as having stress, it should be acknowledged that this is based on my own perception. Instrumental studies have not been conducted. ... Having said so, it seems that stress falls on the first syllable for two- and three-syllable words. Four-syllable root words are unusual in Nmbo; words greater than four syllables are morphologically complex. Stress seems to be attracted by the first syllable with an open vowel, and appears to be assigned at the syllable level. Both characteristics suggest that intensity is a relevant factor in the definition of Nmbo stress. ... The central vowels…
